requirement:
The instructions supplied under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered
page before submitting its answer. They explain how to select the tags of
excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.
Finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.
rationale:
The subject requires the first-search `instructions` text to do four things. It must tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting. It must explain how to select the tags of excerpts used as evidence. It must explain how to pass `used: []` when none contributed. It must say that finishing records the selected inputs without fetching more source.

The only reviewed test is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]`. It is marked `{test}` for the subject. It takes the `instructions` string from the first successful `search_text` result, which has an empty `matches` array, and asserts that the string contains each of these phrases:
- "Before submitting, close every delivered search page" covers the duty to finish every delivered page before submitting.
- "finish_search" names the tool to call.
- "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read" covers how to select tags of excerpts used as evidence.
- "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result" covers passing `used: []` when none contributed.
- "without reading more source" covers the point that finishing fetches no further source.

The test also asserts that the first `search_structure` result in a separate session carries identical instructions. That means the content holds for structural searches as well as text searches. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field. That behavior belongs to the parent requirement `first_search.instructions`, which the test also covers.

The checks are substring assertions, so they do not pin the exact wording. They do enforce every content element the subject names. An instruction text that left out any of those elements would fail. The subject has no other obligations, boundary cases or modes that need separate tests. No acknowledgments apply, and I found no gap.
